newsitem.title: USA: Hispanic buying power soars in United States.
newsitem.headline: Hispanic buying power soars in United States.

text.p: Hispanic buying power has been growing faster than overall consumer purchasing power in the United States since 1990, hitting a pace nearly three times the rate of inflation, a new study said on Thursday.
The University of Georgia's Selig Centre for Economic Growth predicted that Hispanic buying power would reach the $350 billion mark this year, up 65 percent from 1990 when it totalled $211 billion.
Overall U.S. buying power was expected to expand by 41 percent over the same seven-year period, while consumer prices were projected to rise 23 percent.

The study noted that purchasing power for black Americans was higher than for Hispanics, exceeding $470 billion. But the Hispanic growth rate still outstripped the 54 percent rise seen for black consumers.
Blacks accounted for 8 percent and Hispanics for 6 percent of an estimated $5.7 trillion in total U.S. buying power.
The study defined buying power as the total after-tax personal income available to U.S. residents for spending on goods and services.

More than two-thirds of Hispanic buying power was found to be concentrated in California, Texas, New York and Florida. The study also said Hispanic residents of California accounted for almost one-third of all Hispanic purchasing power.
